stem:
Rehan's school has two taps on the same tank. Tap A alone fills the tank in $4$ days. Tap B alone fills the tank in $12$ days. Both taps run together on that tank.

Which claim correctly finds how long they take together?

options.text: The answer is the one-day rate itself, reported as the filling time.
Add the filling times to get $4 + 12 = 16$ days.
The one-day rates are $\dfrac{1}{4}$ and $\dfrac{1}{12}$; together $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of the tank fills per day, so the tank fills in $3$ days.
Adding the one-day rates also gives the fill time when Tap A runs alone for some days and then Tap B runs alone afterward.

teacher.key_rationale: Convert each fill time to a one-day rate: 1/4 + 1/12 = 1/3 tank per day, so time is 3 days. Naming the rate as the time, adding the days, or applying the same sum to sequential work all miss the combined-rate hinge.
